HEEWON STYLE — a premium KOREAN WEBTOON / MANHWA splash illustration of a group, lit with cinematic tenebrism. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). WAIST-UP GROUP SHOT of five, two in front, three behind. DRAW IT EXACTLY IN THE STYLE OF THE ATTACHED CHARACTER SHEET: the same clean confident black ink linework, the same manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair). It must read as an INKED DRAWING: visible line strokes everywhere — bold tapered contour lines around every figure, drawn fold lines in the silk and armour, hair drawn as inked strands, a little cross-hatching and line shading in the shadows — then flat cel-shading in two or three tones per colour, no airbrushed gradients. Each face must be recognisably the character drawn on the sheet, wearing the same clothes. NOT realistic, NOT an oil painting, NOT photoreal, NOT painterly, NOT a 3D render, no skin pores or photographic texture. ONLY THESE FIVE PEOPLE in the frame. THE DEFECTORS: MEN WHO LAID DOWN THEIR ARMS AND TOOK THE OTHER COUNTRY'S RANK. In front, each offering his sword hilt-first toward the camera: the Gaya prince Muryuk, head bowed, his conical helm under his other arm; and Yeon Namsan, a Goguryeo noble, kneeling, eyes lifted. Behind them, three more men in pure black silhouette, only their outstretched sword hilts catching the light. One cold light from above. Any sword is the ancient straight Korean ring-pommel dao: a small iron ring pommel, a short wrapped grip, a thin metal band and NO hand guard, a perfectly straight blade — never a katana, never a tsuba. CHARACTER SHEET (copy these faces, hair and clothes exactly): LEFT of the sheet = KIM MURYUK; RIGHT of the sheet = YEON NAMSAN. KIM MURYUK — Look: Square weathered Gaya face, heavy brows, long pauses in the eyes; grows grey, then white, but never bald under the helm. Dress: Out of battle: plain dark Gaya-cut po with a purple sash; his Gaya helm (rounded iron bowl, wide flared brim, tall red horsehair cone) on his head or under his arm, ALWAYS, even indoors at home (it sits on a stand by the door at night). Now: Very old: white beard, a stick, four blankets, the helm still on. Colour #8B5CF6. | YEON NAMSAN Colour #d4776a. LIGHT AND BACKGROUND (deep manhwa tenebrism, darker than a normal splash page): about TWO-THIRDS OF THE FRAME IS PURE INK-BLACK. No set, no architecture or floor beyond what the scene names, no props beyond what the characters hold. Each figure is pulled out of the black by ONE hard, narrow key light from the side or from below in THAT PERSON'S OWN COLOUR, catching only a cheekbone, an eye, the bridge of the nose, the edge of a sleeve, a plate of armour or a hand; the rest of each figure falls off into solid black shadow and merges with the background, so neighbouring figures are separated only by their coloured edge light. MOSTLY IN DARKNESS: each figure is about TWO-THIRDS BLACK SILHOUETTE; only the side of the face, shoulder, hands and robe edge turned toward that person's own light show colour and detail, the rest merges into the black. SPLIT LIGHTING ON EVERY FIGURE: the lit side of each face and body in that person's colour, the other half PURE BLACK; no even front light, no fill light, no evenly lit robes — even white silk falls to black on its shadow side. Faces readable but half in shadow, eyes catching the light (ordinary eyes — no light streaks or glow across the eyes). At most a few thin wisps of smoke tinted by those coloured lights. Deep inky blacks, crisp highlights, hard cast shadows. Each person's colour is the colour of the light on them — never a glow aura, halo or outline glow. BLOCKING, BODY LANGUAGE AND FACIAL EXPRESSIONS show who they are to each other at a glance. Faces and clothes from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. One of each person, never cloned. No text, no lettering, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
